providers.name: local_c1_extension
providers.assessment: The finite C1 locus is open; compact thickening supplies delta>0. The bump has inner radius R+delta/3 and outer radius R+2delta/3, so its support lies inside the good larger closed ball. The product is C1 there and locally zero outside the support. It equals F as a germ at every selected closed-ball point, enough for both derivatives and boundary values. Consumed by the public successor branch.

providers.name: divergence_continuous
providers.assessment: Rewrites the literal lineDeriv sum to the actual fderiv trace using differentiability and proves continuity by finite summation of continuously evaluated derivative components. Used for divergence_integrable.

providers.name: compact_divergence_integral
providers.assessment: Actually transports F through the PiLp equivalence, derives C1 and compact support of G, calls the existing compact-field whole-space producer and consumes its hzero via volume_preserving_toLp. No new whole-space zero-integral premise is introduced. Used by scalar_cutoff_integral.

providers.name: divergence_integrable
providers.assessment: Continuity plus compact support of fderiv, followed by the trace map taking 0 to 0, gives genuine Integrable of coordinateDivergence. Used by scalar_cutoff_integral and compact_ball_flux.

providers.name: polar_integral
providers.assessment: Positive ambient dimension n+1 only. Removes the null origin, transports Integrable through the actual sphere/radius homeomorphism, invokes Fubini with that Integrable witness, and unfolds volumeIoiPow n to the positive radial density r^n. No arbitrary surface-normalization substitution. Used by cutoff_flux_identity.

providers.name: radial_flux_integrable
providers.assessment: Actual continuous scalar pairing on the compact unit sphere is integrable for finite volume.toSphere, for each real parameter r. Used by compact_ball_flux.

providers.name: radial_flux_continuous
providers.assessment: Joint continuity and compact parameter integration prove continuity of the actual radial integral; multiplying by r^(dimension-1) is continuous. Used in the shrinking-shell limit.

providers.name: shellProfile
providers.assessment: Literal profile 1-q((s-R^2)/((R+epsilon)^2-R^2)); total scalar division is harmless, while all shell-use identities later impose R>0 and epsilon>0.

providers.name: shellCutoff
providers.assessment: Literal composition of shellProfile with squared distance from a. No predicate or default-valued flux object is substituted.

providers.name: shellProfile_smooth
providers.assessment: Actual smooth-transition composition and division by a constant give C2, including degenerate denominator values as total functions. Used for cutoff smoothness, derivative continuity, and radial calculus.

providers.name: shellCutoff_smooth
providers.assessment: Composition with smooth squared norm gives C2 everywhere. Used for product-rule regularity and dominated-convergence measurability.

providers.name: shellCutoff_bounds
providers.assessment: Derives 0<=chi<=1 from the actual transition bounds for all parameters. Used to dominate chi*divF and in the scalar integral identity.

providers.name: shellCutoff_one
providers.assessment: For R,epsilon>0 the squared shell width is positive; points of the selected closed ball have transition argument <=0 and chi=1. Used for the volume limit.

providers.name: shellCutoff_zero
providers.assessment: For norm(x-a)>=R+epsilon the transition argument is >=1 and chi=0. Used for the volume limit.

providers.name: shellProfile_bounds
providers.assessment: Same actual transition bounds in scalar profile form. Used to obtain derivative zero at the constant-region endpoints by local extrema.

providers.name: shellProfile_deriv
providers.assessment: Differentiates the literal composition by the chain rule, with the exact negative sign and denominator. Used for shell-weight nonnegativity.

providers.name: shellWeight
providers.assessment: Literal -(2*r*profile'(r^2)); under positive shell width this is (2*r/D)*q'((r^2-R^2)/D). This is a real derivative, not an assumed radial density.

providers.name: shellWeight_continuous
providers.assessment: C2 profile makes its derivative continuous, hence the actual weight is continuous. Used for scalar FTC and interval integrability in the limit.

providers.name: shellWeight_nonneg
providers.assessment: For r>=0 and R,epsilon>0, monotonicity of the actual transition and positive denominator give nonnegative weight. No sign assertion is used at negative radii.

providers.name: shellWeight_derivative
providers.assessment: The weight is the actual derivative of -profile(t^2). Chain-rule coefficient 2*t and negative sign match the definition. Used by scalar FTC.

providers.name: shellWeight_mass
providers.assessment: Scalar FTC with the continuous actual weight and transition endpoint values proves mass exactly 1 over R..R+epsilon. Used by shellWeight_limit.

providers.name: shellWeight_zero_inner
providers.assessment: For 0<=r<=R the profile at r^2 is its global maximum 1, giving actual derivative zero even at the endpoint. Used for radial support restriction.

providers.name: shellWeight_zero_outer
providers.assessment: For r>=R+epsilon the profile is its global minimum 0, giving actual derivative zero even at the endpoint. Used for radial support restriction.

providers.name: shellWeight_limit
providers.assessment: For positive epsilon, uses weight mass 1 and nonnegativity to bound the error by local oscillation of continuous H near R. It does not posit an epsilon-uniform bound for the singular shell density. Used by compact_ball_flux.

providers.name: divergence_scalar_product
providers.assessment: Differentiates chi*F and sums matching-coordinate derivative components; the remaining sum is the actual gradient pairing. The real inner-product symmetry is justified. Used in scalar_cutoff_integral.

providers.name: scalar_cutoff_integral
providers.assessment: Derives Integrable of div(chi F), chi divF and then their actual difference cross term before using integral_add. The old compact-field producer supplies zero integral for div(chi F). Used by cutoff_flux_identity.

providers.name: cutoff_sphere_pairing
providers.assessment: Uses the actual radial_gradient_laplacian gradient clause. norm(r*zeta)^2=r^2 for unit zeta even for negative r, and the resulting sign/coefficient are exactly shellWeight times <F,zeta>. Used by cutoff_flux_identity.

providers.name: cutoff_volume_limit
providers.assessment: In positive dimension the exceptional sphere is volume-null. The actual cutoff products are measurable and bounded by globally L1 norm(D); away from the sphere they eventually equal the ball indicator times D. Genuine dominated convergence yields the open-ball integral. Used by compact_ball_flux.

providers.name: cutoff_flux_identity
providers.assessment: Translates the genuinely L1 cross term by a, applies the literal polar law, uses the radial pairing identity, and restricts positive radii to the shell using proven weight support. Exact exponent n corresponds to ambient n+1. Used by compact_ball_flux.

providers.name: compact_ball_flux
providers.assessment: Combines separately derived volume and sphere L1 with equality of the volume and shell limits. Filter nhdsGT 0 is nontrivial. Used by the public successor branch.

providers.name: gradient_c1
providers.assessment: Under actual local C2, fderiv_right is locally C1; inverse Riesz continuous linear equivalence preserves this. Used by divergence_gradient and the public ball-flux application.

providers.name: divergence_gradient
providers.assessment: Differentiates the complete gradient-component identity. Both gradient and derivative-map differentiability come from local C2. Evaluating the actual second Frechet derivative on each Euclidean basis diagonal matches the pinned Laplacian trace formula. Used to make the actual volume integrand zero.

findings.observation: The lesson explicitly includes n=0 but typesets n-1 and S^(n-1) without spelling out the theorem's natural-subtraction convention or the empty unit sphere in R^0. The scoped source packet and Lean statement are explicit about truncated subtraction.
findings.recommendation: For lossless standalone reader notation, add that n-1 is natural subtraction and that at n=0 the unit sphere is empty and tau=0, or separately display the positive-dimensional formula and zero-dimensional branch.
findings.reason_nonblocking: The current reader already states divF=0 and tau=0 at n=0. Even an ordinary R^(-1) reading gives the same zero right side for R>0, so this does not falsify the theorem or alter a premise. It is a reader-notation clarification, not a mathematical source repair.
